summary: The Polestar 2 is a premium electric fastback that Australian reviewers consistently praise as a genuine driver's car — crisp steering, tidy body control and, in the rear-drive Long Range Single Motor, a 659km WLTP range that beats most rivals in this price band. Where opinion splits is liveability: the ride is judged disciplined by some and outright punishing by others, and nearly everyone marks down the cramped rear seat, a legacy of the combustion-derived platform it shares with the Volvo XC40. Production of this generation ended in China in October 2026 and it is now sold from remaining stock ahead of a clean-sheet successor due in 2027, which means discounting today and correspondingly weak resale tomorrow.
pros: 659km WLTP range from the Long Range Single Motor — more than a BYD Seal Premium (570km) or a Polestar 4 Single Motor (620km), though short of the Tesla Model 3 Long Range RWD's 750km
Rated a driver's car by CarExpert and Chasing Cars alike: crisp, direct steering and excellent body control that the softer Model 3 does not match
MY26 update lifted DC fast charging to 205kW on the 82kWh pack and fitted a much quicker Qualcomm infotainment processor, fixing the range's most-criticised software lag
Rated braked towing of 1500kg, which most electric sedans in this price band do not offer at all
5-year unlimited-kilometre warranty and 5-star ANCAP, with well-tuned driver-assist calibration reviewers do not complain about
cons: Ride is firm to the point of being abrupt over sharp bumps — Chasing Cars called it 'considerably firmer than you expect' for a premium car, and this is the single most repeated criticism across Australian reviews
Cramped rear seat: a high floor from the battery, an unsupportive bench, small windows and a wasted transmission tunnel from the shared combustion platform — a couple's car more than a family one
407-litre boot is well short of the Tesla Model 3's 594 litres, and the panoramic roof has no blind
Costly options creep: a heat pump requires the $1500 Climate pack and a power tailgate the $4700 Plus pack, so a well-equipped car lands well above the list price

Run-out model: production ended in October 2026, the car is sold from pre-configured stock (a $5,000-off drive-away offer runs to 31 December 2026) and an all-new Polestar 2 is due in 2027 — resale should be expected to be soft
